scope: One-session JoyAI full-stream robot replacement with a hand-held florist-scissors contract
summary: A generated scissors-bearing robot reference plus an explicit rigid-tool prompt produces a 665-frame JoyAI proposal and an exact 660-frame final timeline. Native review sees a black/silver tool following the hand through the source trimming interval, but its two handle rings and finger-through-ring state are not independently separable in every required frame, so the tool gate is not promoted.
evidence: The retained successful run generates 665 frames in one session in 105.6918576513417 seconds, or 6.29187540816734 generated frames per second.
Finalization trims only five cloned causal tail frames, restores the 16-pixel source borders without rescaling, and verifies 660 frames at 1280x720, 24 fps, and 27.5 seconds.
The conditioning image is recorded as semantic reference only; it is never counted as evidence about the generated video.
The first generation attempt is retained as PARTIAL because the remote reference path was absent; the second attempt succeeded only after hash-addressed reference transfer.
lessons: Small manipulated tools need a separate timeline/topology contract and native-resolution human veto; a prompt alone can collapse scissors into a metallic line or a finger texture.
Remote proposal generation must preflight the reference file before reserving an expensive model session.
limitations: Native frames do not resolve both handle rings and finger-through-ring occupancy throughout the interval.
The result is synthetic visual evidence and does not establish metric pose, torque, force, or force closure.
next_actions: Train or attach an independently tracked rigid-tool layer before enabling automatic tool promotion.
